plan.question_en: Design a planar ZnS/ZnSe multilayer coating on a Germanium substrate to maximize LWIR (8000-11000 nm) transmittance and minimize MWIR (3000-5000 nm) transmittance for a cooled HgCdTe detector, subject to layer count and material constraints.

facets.ask: Find complete design cases for ZnS/ZnSe stacks on Ge targeting LWIR transmission and MWIR rejection.
keyword_queries: ZnS ZnSe multilayer coating germanium substrate LWIR MWIR filter design

facets.ask: Seek specific application contexts involving cooled detectors and thermal background suppression.
question_queries: How to design a cold shield filter for HgCdTe detectors using ZnS and ZnSe layers to block 3-5 micron radiation?

facets.ask: Retrieve accurate n and k data for the relevant IR bands to ensure realistic modeling of absorption and index contrast.
keyword_queries: optical constants ZnS ZnSe germanium 3 micron 11 micron extinction coefficient

facets.ask: Identify synthesis techniques for sharp cutoffs under strict layer-count constraints.
question_queries: What optimization methods allow steep spectral transitions between MWIR and LWIR with fewer than 20 dielectric layers?

facets.ask: Understand fundamental material limits that might prevent 'as high as possible' transmittance regardless of coating design.
question_queries: How does the absorption edge of ZnSe and ZnS limit transmittance in the 8-11 micron range?

task_sheet.user_objective: Design a planar ZnS/ZnSe multilayer coating on a Germanium substrate to maximize LWIR (8000-11000 nm) transmittance and minimize MWIR (3000-5000 nm) transmittance for a cooled HgCdTe detector, subject to layer count and material constraints.

subgoals.original_span: 需要该波段尽可能高的透过率
subgoals.operational_definition: Wavelength integral of transmittance over 8000-11000 nm divided by band width, for unpolarized light at 0 degrees incidence into a semi-infinite Ge exit medium.

subgoals.objective: Minimize mid-wave infrared transmittance to suppress thermal background
subgoals.original_span: 尽可能抑制 3000-5000 nm 中波红外的热背景辐射
subgoals.operational_definition: Wavelength integral of transmittance over 3000-5000 nm divided by band width, for unpolarized light at 0 degrees incidence into a semi-infinite Ge exit medium. Minimizing transmission here reduces flux reaching the detector from the warm side.

application_intents.intent: Cooled HgCdTe infrared focal plane detector window
application_intents.original_span: 制冷型碲镉汞红外焦平面探测器

application_intents.intent: Reduce thermal load on the focal plane by blocking MWIR radiation
application_intents.operational_definition: Motivation for minimizing MWIR transmittance; no explicit heat-load calculation or temperature-weighted metric is defined in this sheet.

application_intents.intent: Report power transmission into the semi-infinite Ge exit substrate
application_intents.operational_definition: Transmission is defined as optical flux entering the semi-infinite Ge substrate, excluding rear-surface effects of a finite window.

goal_relationships.coupling: G1 and G2 are spectrally adjacent goals for the same coating stack; maximizing transmission in one band while minimizing it in another creates a sharp spectral edge requirement that may couple layer thickness sensitivities.

explicit_constraints.constraint: Coating materials: Only ZnS and ZnSe
explicit_constraints.original_span: 仅使用 ZnS 和 ZnSe
膜系总层数不超过 16 层

known_data.statement: Application involves a cooled HgCdTe detector
known_data.original_span: 制冷型碲镉汞红外焦平面探测器

unknowns_assumptions.statement: Execution assumes 0 degree incidence, equal-s/p unpolarized light, and wavelength-integral means as per protocol, though not explicitly stated in the original question.
The Ge substrate is treated as a semi-infinite exit medium for the planar-stack calculation; rear surface conditions and substrate thickness are not modeled.

Optical constants (n, k) dispersion data sources and specific values for ZnS, ZnSe, and Ge in these bands are not provided; extinction coefficients (k) must be verified as non-zero where physically appropriate.
Operating temperature, exact detector geometry, and rear-surface anti-reflection conditions are unspecified.
No global user thickness bounds or fabrication tolerances were specified; model-proposed domains will be used.
Unverified model interpretation (not user-provided or accepted truth; original_span is not an exact native-question quote): Target bands are LWIR atmospheric window and MWIR thermal background

research_questions.question: What are effective ZnS/ZnSe multilayer designs for LWIR high-transmission and MWIR blocking on Ge substrates?
How do material absorption edges and refractive index contrasts of ZnS and ZnSe affect performance in the 3-11 micron range?
Which optimization strategies can achieve steep spectral edges between MWIR and LWIR with limited layer counts (<16)?

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Quarter-wave stack interference using high/low index contrast between ZnSe and ZnS to create a stopband in MWIR and passband in LWIR.
Material intrinsic absorption limits may constrain maximum achievable transmittance if not accounted for in design.

task_sheet.original_question: 我负责制冷型碲镉汞红外焦平面探测器的长波红外窗口膜层研发。探测器工作在 8000-11000 nm 长波红外大气窗口，需要该波段尽可能高的透过率，同时尽可能抑制 3000-5000 nm 中波红外的热背景辐射，以降低焦平面的热负载。请在空气入射、锗（Ge）基底条件下，仅使用 ZnS 和 ZnSe 设计一个平面多层介质膜，膜系总层数不超过 16 层。
